questions.q: Under PD 957, what is the minimum lot area for an "Open Market" Single Detached house?
questions.n: This is the highest minimum lot area requirement for single-detached units under PD 957.

questions.q: Under PD 957, what is the minimum lot area for a "Medium Cost" Single Detached house?
questions.n: Medium Cost housing is categorized just below Open Market in PD 957 standards.

questions.q: Under BP 220, what is the minimum lot area for "Economic Housing" (Single Detached)?
questions.n: This is the legal minimum specifically designated for the Economic category under BP 220.

questions.q: Under BP 220, what is the minimum lot area for "Socialized Housing" (Single Detached)?
questions.n: This is the absolute minimum lot area for a single-detached unit in a socialized subdivision.

questions.q: What is the minimum front setback for a PD 957 residential unit?
questions.n: PD 957 maintains more generous setback standards compared to BP 220.

questions.q: What is the minimum front setback for a BP 220 residential unit?
questions.n: BP 220 allows for smaller setbacks to maximize land utilization for affordable housing.

questions.q: What is the minimum road width for a major road in a PD 957 subdivision?
questions.n: Major roads in standard subdivisions must accommodate wider right-of-ways.

questions.q: What is the minimum road width for a major road in a BP 220 subdivision?
questions.n: BP 220 allows for narrower major roads compared to high-end subdivisions.

questions.q: For a 1-hectare subdivision under PD 957, what percentage of the area is required for "Parks and Playgrounds"?
questions.n: The percentage for parks is variable based on the density (units per hectare).

questions.q: In BP 220, what is the minimum floor area for an Economic housing unit?
questions.n: Economic units must provide slightly more space than socialized units.

questions.q: What is the "Turning Torso" known for in terms of structure?
o: It is the first "twisting" skyscraper in the world.
It is the first building with a double-skin facade.
It is the tallest building in Europe.
It was the first skyscraper built entirely of timber.
questions.n: The design by Calatrava rotates 90 degrees from base to tip.

questions.q: Frank Lloyd Wright's "Usonian" houses were designed for which group of people?
questions.n: Usonian houses were intended to be affordable, decentralized, and uniquely American.

questions.q: What is "Le Modulor"?
o: A musical theory regarding space and sound.
An anthropometric scale of proportions developed by Le Corbusier.
A modular housing system for post-war reconstruction.
questions.n: It uses the human body and mathematics (Golden Ratio) to standardize architectural dimensions.

questions.q: Who is the architect of the "Fallingwater" house?
questions.n: This house is a masterpiece of Organic Architecture, built over a waterfall.

questions.q: What material did Ludwig Mies van der Rohe famously use in the Barcelona Pavilion to create a sense of luxury and flow?
questions.n: These exotic materials provided texture and color to the minimalist plan.

questions.q: In the Renaissance, what was the "Golden Section" used for?
o: To calculate the structural stability of arches.
To divide the floor plan between masters and servants.
To determine the tax value of a building.
To achieve aesthetically pleasing proportions based on the ratio 1:1.618.
questions.n: This mathematical ratio was believed to reflect the divine order of the universe.

questions.q: Which SPP document outlines the "Full-time Supervision" services?
questions.n: Specifically handles the architect's role in full-time project supervision.

questions.q: What is the "Specialty Permit" often used for?
o: For temporary structures like scaffolding, sidewalks, or specialized installations not covered by ancillary permits.
questions.n: These are issued for works that are either temporary or unique in nature.

questions.q: What is the minimum area of a "Socialized Housing" lot for a Rowhouse?
questions.n: Rowhouses have the smallest lot area requirement in the BP 220 socialized category.

questions.q: What is the "Building Permit Exception" for minor repairs?
o: Repairs that do not involve structural members and do not exceed a certain cost (often 5,000 PHP depending on local rules).
Repairs that cost less than 50,000 PHP.
Painting and tiling regardless of cost.
Any repair to a residential house.
questions.n: Safety is the priority; structural work ALWAYS requires a permit.

questions.q: What is the "Cite Industrielle"?
o: A theoretical plan for an industrial city designed by Tony Garnier.
questions.n: It was a pioneering concept that separated zones for living, working, and leisure.

questions.q: What is "Garden City" as proposed by Ebenezer Howard?
o: A city where all buildings are covered in plants.
A city with a large central park.
A city solely dedicated to agriculture.
A method of urban planning in which self-contained communities are surrounded by "greenbelts."
questions.n: It aimed to combine the best of the city and the country.

questions.q: Who designed the "City of Tomorrow" (Ville Contemporaine)?
questions.n: His plan featured massive high-rises to house millions, surrounded by parks.

questions.q: Which architect said "Less is more"?
questions.n: This is the definitive slogan of 20th-century minimalism.

questions.q: Which architect said "Less is a bore"?
questions.n: This quote signaled the rise of Post-Modernism and the return of complexity.

questions.q: What is the "Radiant City"?
o: A city powered entirely by solar energy.
An unrealized urban design by Le Corbusier featuring high-rise housing in a park-like setting.
A city in Florida designed for the sun.
questions.n: The 'Ville Radieuse' was an evolution of his earlier urban theories.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of the National Building Code (PD 1096)?
o: To manage the licensing of architects.
To dictate the architectural style of the country.
To provide minimum standards and requirements for all buildings to ensure safety and public welfare.
questions.n: It sets the baseline for fire safety, structural integrity, and sanitation.

questions.q: What is a "Setback"?
o: The height of a building step-back.
The required distance between the building and the property line.
The area behind the building only.
questions.n: Setbacks ensure light, ventilation, and fire separation between structures.

questions.q: What is "R-1" occupancy?
questions.n: R-1 refers to low-density, typically detached, single-family dwellings.

questions.q: What is "R-5" occupancy?
questions.n: R-5 represents the highest density residential zone, often for high-rise residential buildings.

questions.q: In professional practice, what does "PCC" stand for?
questions.n: This is the benchmark value used to calculate percentage-based fees.

questions.q: Under SPP 202, who pays for the geotechnical (soil) test?
questions.n: All specialized site data (surveys, soil tests) are the financial responsibility of the client.

questions.q: If an architect provides "Consultation" services only, what is the usual compensation?
o: Per hour or per session rate.
A fixed fee per square meter.
Lump sum for the whole year.
questions.n: Consultation is a time-based service requiring expert advice rather than drawings.

questions.q: What is the "Professional Fee" for a Residential project (Group 1) under the old UAP guidelines?
questions.n: Residential projects are considered high-complexity (Group 1), warranting this standard fee.

questions.q: What is the fee for "Repeat Buildings" (identical designs)?
o: A single fee for all buildings regardless of how many.
The fee decreases for each subsequent unit (e.g., 100% for 1st, 80% for 2nd, etc.).
The same fee for every building.
The architect is paid only for the first building.
questions.n: This accounts for the reduced effort in the design phase for identical structures.

questions.q: What is the minimum width of a "Chaflan" for a road wider than 3.6m?
questions.n: The chaflan (corner cut) must be 4 meters when both intersecting roads are wider than 3.6 meters.

questions.q: What is the maximum width of a driveway for a single-family house?
questions.n: This width allows for comfortable vehicle entry while limiting the impact on the sidewalk.

questions.q: What is the meaning of "BP 220"?
o: The Socialized and Economic Housing Law.
questions.n: It was enacted to provide standards for affordable housing projects.

questions.q: What is the meaning of "PD 957"?
o: The Subdivision and Condominium Buyer's Protective Decree.
questions.n: It regulates the sale and development of commercial subdivisions and condominiums.

questions.q: Who is the architect of the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum in New York?
questions.n: The museum is famous for its spiraling ramp and organic form.

questions.q: Which architect is known for the "TWA Flight Center" and its organic, bird-like shell?
questions.n: His 'Neo-Expressionist' work used concrete shells to mimic the motion of flight.

questions.q: What is the "Brutalism" style known for?
o: The use of bright, pastel colors.
Raw, exposed concrete (Béton brut) and massive, rugged forms.
questions.n: The term comes from the French for 'raw concrete'.

questions.q: Which building in the Philippines is a prime example of Brutalism?
o: The National Museum of Fine Arts
Cultural Center of the Philippines (Leandro Locsin).
questions.n: Its massive block of concrete appearing to float over a plaza is a landmark of the style.

questions.q: What is the minimum width of a PWD-accessible parking slot?
questions.n: The extra width (1.20m more than standard) allows for wheelchair maneuverability beside the car.

questions.q: What is the maximum slope of a ramp for PWD access (BP 344)?
questions.n: This is the legal maximum to ensure safety and ease of use.

questions.q: What is the "Occupant Load"?
o: The total number of staff members in a building.
The weight of the people on the floor.
The amount of furniture in a room.
The maximum number of people allowed in a space based on its area and use.
questions.n: It is used to calculate the required number of exits and plumbing fixtures.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a "Firewall"?
o: To prevent the spread of fire between adjacent properties.
To provide a place for graffiti.
questions.n: It must have a high fire-resistive rating and no openings.

questions.q: In ancient Greece, what was the "Agora"?
o: The central public marketplace and meeting space.
questions.n: It was the heart of the city's commercial and political life.

questions.q: In Roman architecture, what was the "Pantheon" built for?
o: As a tomb for the Emperor.
As a temple to all the gods.
questions.n: The name literally means 'all gods'.

questions.q: Who said "God is in the details"?
questions.n: This reflects his commitment to structural precision and minimalist perfection.
